title: Audit event change-skein and actor fingerprint specification for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Define a compact, tamper-evident event shape and taxonomy for admin/change events in RBAC v2 that captures actor identity provenance (SSO/SAML-linked), target fingerprints, and an append-only change-skein encoding for minimal yet reconstructable deltas. Goal is to support fast audit lookups, efficient storage for high-volume admin activity, and clear evidence for compliance reviews without leaking sensitive attributes.
scope: This ticket covers the canonical event schema, a change-skein encoding (hash-linked change frames), actor fingerprinting rules (how to represent SSO/SAML actors and linking to org identities), target object fingerprint strategy, field-level redaction guidance, retention class tags, and search/indexing knobs for the Console. Implementation and storage format (Kafka message envelope + GCS archival) are covered as acceptance criteria but not part of this ticket's code deliverable.
background: We currently have multiple audit encodings across services with inconsistent actor fields and oversized payloads for admin ops. This causes slow queries for security investigations, storage bloat, and uncertainty about what minimal fields must be retained for compliance audits. RBAC v2 introduces role inheritance and transient admin sessions (impersonation, delegation) which complicate actor provenance. SSO/SAML links must be preserved for external identity proofs.
proposal_summary: Introduce a compact event envelope with: 1) top-level metadata (event_type, ts, tenant_id, retention_class), 2) an actor_fingerprint (stable, hashed linking to identity_graph), 3) actor_provenance_chain (ordered list of external_assertions as strings), 4) change_skein: an ordered array of change_frames where each frame is a small map encoded as a canonical JSON string plus a SHA-256 pointer to the previous frame (hashlink), and 5) target_fingerprint + target_annotations (read-only identifiers, types, and non-sensitive selectors). Provide field-level redaction markers and an audit-level confidence score for automated enrichers.
acceptance_criteria: Schema draft in JSON Schema format (flattened canonical keys) committed to security-audit-v2/specs in the repo
Compact change_skein encoding description with example payloads for common admin flows (role grant, role revoke, policy mutation, SSO mapping) included
Actor fingerprint algorithm defined (inputs, hashing salt strategy, rotation guidance) and documented for SDKs
Redaction policy enumerated with examples (PII removal vs. retention for compliance) and placeholder markers in schema
Search and indexing suggestions for Console (which fields to index, suggested composite keys, and retention tiers) documented
Performance target: average query time for 30-day admin hunt queries < 800ms on existing analytics stack (benchmarked)
out_of_scope: Implementing storage lifecycle jobs, migration of legacy events, or the UI surface beyond index/field guidance. Those will be follow-up tickets.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: We prioritize compactness and deterministic canonicalization over including full object snapshots — snapshots increase storage but simplify forensics. The change_skein plus replay helpers provide a middle ground.

Actor fingerprints protect against accidental exposure of SAML assertions, but introduce a need for a fingerprint resolution service when full identity context is required. We'll rely on an internal identity_graph service with ACLs for resolutions.
Hashlink chaining makes events tamper-evident and allows efficient append-only verification, but adds complexity to downstream consumers (they need to validate chain integrity when needed).
Field-level redaction reduces privacy risk but may hamper future automated investigations; redaction markers with reason codes help auditors understand missing data.
implementation_notes: Canonicalization must use stable key ordering (alphabetical) and UTF-8 normalization for strings. The change_frame payloads should be canonical JSON strings before hashing. Use SHA-256 (hex) for hashlinks and record the hashing_algorithm field in the event. Actor fingerprint input tuple: [issuer, external_id, assertion_id, tenant_id] salted with per-org salt from KMS. Store fingerprints in a separate thin lookup index to avoid repeated expansion in hot queries.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Emit dual-encoded events for 30 days (legacy envelope + new compact envelope) for all admin-changing endpoints. Phase 2: Backfill indexers to consume compact envelope, run consistency checks. Phase 3: Deprecate legacy envelope after 90 days with migration report. Each phase gates require schema regression tests and an opt-in tenant pilot.
risks: Leaking SSO/SAML assertions if actor_provenance_chain is not properly redacted—mitigate by storing only assertion metadata strings, not the raw assertion, unless explicitly permitted.
Fingerprint collision risk is low but non-zero; include collision detection and rotation policy in identity_graph service.
Query performance regressions if too many fields are indexed—recommend controlled indexing and analytics rollups.
